I've practiced meditation daily for twenty years. When my daughter asked me to teach her, I couldn't explain why certain techniques worked. I'd been doing them mechanically, never understanding the principles. Teaching her forced me to study what I thought I'd mastered decades ago.

CANDIDATE A:
I've driven manual transmission cars my whole life. Trying to teach my nephew, I realized I couldn't articulate the clutch-gas relationship. My body knew, but my mind didn't. His confusion revealed that I drive by feel, not by understanding.

CANDIDATE B:
I've practiced meditation daily for twenty years. When my daughter asked me to teach her, I found I could explain exactly why each technique works—where the attention goes, how the breath settles the mind. Teaching her only confirmed how deeply I'd come to understand the practice.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:59"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both involve realizing a lack of understanding when trying to teach something they thought they had mastered."}
